home.seo_description: A user template for quickly building exhibition, archive, and record-centered websites.
home.title: A gallery template that connects exhibitions and records
home.lead: A public-site example for calmly browsing works, exhibitions, archives, and written notes.
home.featured_title: Records of where the light passed
home.featured_body: The featured exhibition presents title, period, space, and curatorial point of view in one readable area. Visitors can understand context and browsing direction before scanning images.
home.featured_location: Space: Main gallery and online archive
home.featured_format: Format: Work introductions, installation records, artist notes
home.archive_title: Archive categories ready for operators to expand
home.archive_one_body: Works, installation photos, press material, and curatorial notes are grouped by exhibition so past shows remain easy to revisit.
home.archive_two_body: Artist profiles, participation history, work lists, and interviews are connected into a deeper browsing path.
home.archive_three_body: Images, manuscripts, links, and conservation notes are separated by management type to reduce operational friction.
home.collection_one_body: Representative images and work descriptions are paired with concise background and collecting criteria.
home.collection_two_body: Planning documents, installation photos, and collaboration records from exhibition preparation are presented as one group.
home.collection_three_body: Public research memos, links, and reference material become readable supporting records.
home.notes_title: Sentences that remain after an exhibition closes
home.notes_body: The record notes area is a home entry point for durable texts such as curatorial essays, field notes, and conservation records.
home.note_one_body: Opening sentences and criteria for reading works give visitors a reason to return.
home.note_two_body: Information from installation, photography, and deinstallation is turned into record-centered content.
home.about_title: A first screen for small galleries and archive projects
home.about_body: This home layout presents exhibitions, archives, collections, and notes with static content first, then can expand into board and page data later.
home.featured_empty_subtitle: Published exhibition data will appear here when it is available.
home.featured_empty_body: There is no currently available exhibition, but the archive and record notes remain browsable.

research_notes.title: Research Notes

press_release.title: Press Release Text

curator_note.summary: A curator note written to read works, documents, and installation records inside one exhibition context.

material_reading.body: Artwork records and archive materials are positioned as evidence that explain one another. Each item is independent while also becoming a clue for rereading the exhibition.

archive_afterlife.body: What remains after closing is not only a work list, but field decisions, lighting records, sentences, and preservation notes. This note passes those relationships to the next reader.

field_note.title: Installation Week Field Note

pale_grid.credit_line: Courtesy of the artist and Glitter Gallery Bz

installation_axis.title: Installation Axis Record
installation_axis.subtitle: Installation material preserving placement and movement

press_fragment.subtitle: Document material for rereading exhibition language

press_fragment.curator_note: The press text shows the difference between the first public explanation and later record language.

installation_photo_set.summary: Installation photographs for reading the structure of the exhibition space and relationships between works.

lighting_plan.title: Lighting Plan Record
lighting_plan.subtitle: A field record of brightness and direction by work
lighting_plan.summary: Field notes for reviewing lighting direction and brightness by artwork.

press_release.subtitle: Public explanation document from the exhibition opening
press_release.summary: A public document showing how the exhibition was first explained externally.
press_release.description: The press release is the first public document of the exhibition language. It remains a reference point for reading differences between curator notes and later archive sentences.
